Renaissance Capital LLC is an American investment management and research firm based in Stamford, Connecticut, specializing in initial public offering (IPO) research and investment products. Founded in 1991 by William K. Smith, Linda Killian, and Kathleen Shelton Smith, the firm provides institutional research services and manages two exchange-traded funds focused on newly public companies. As of March 13, 2025, the firm had $157 million in discretionary assets under management.
History
Renaissance Capital was founded in 1991 by William K. Smith, Linda Killian, and Kathleen Shelton Smith, who became acquainted at the Wharton School in the 1970s. Their IPO Intelligence research platform provides institutional investors with comprehensive pre-IPO research and models on US and international IPOs.
In the fall of 1996, Renaissance Capital launched their website, www.ipohome.com. By 1999 it became the largest active website on the Internet for free IPO research, averaging 70,000 hits per day. By February 2000, this number grew to 500,000 hits per day.
In 1997 Renaissance Capital launched the first mutual fund to invest mainly in IPOs. Within three months of being established, the fund had 1,500 investors. Billionaire Mario Gabelli, founder of Gabelli Asset Management Company Investors, commented "it takes a reasonable amount of time for small, even large, companies to get 1,000 shareholders, so I think they are on a fast track."
In 2001, the co-founders published "IPOs for Everyone: The 12 Secrets of Investing in IPOs" through John Wiley & Sons.
Renaissance Capital partnered with FTSE Group in 2005 to create the FTSE Renaissance IPO Index Series, which tracks the performance of newly public companies. In 2011, the partnership was expanded and the series was renamed the FTSE Renaissance Global IPO Index Series to include international markets.
On March 6, 2012, Kathleen Shelton Smith provided expert testimony to the United States Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs for the "Spurring Job Growth through Capital Formation while Protecting Investors, Part II." hearing. The hearing focused on legislation regarding IPOs and fundraising for startups and existing businesses, which ultimately led to the creation of the JOBS Act.
The firm launched the Renaissance IPO ETF (ticker: IPO) on October 14, 2013, on the NYSE Arca exchange. This was followed by the Renaissance International IPO ETF (ticker: IPOS) on October 6, 2014.
In 2017, Renaissance Capital introduced IPO Pro, a retail subscription-based platform providing IPO market data and analysis.
Organization
Renaissance Capital operates as a privately held limited liability company. Kathleen Shelton Smith serves as Chairman and William K. Smith serves as Chief Executive Officer, with each owning more than 25% of the firm.
Products and Services
IPO Intelligence
IPO Intelligence is Renaissance Capital's institutional research service, providing analysis and data on initial public offerings to institutional investors including mutual funds, hedge funds, and pension plans.
IPO Pro
IPO Pro is a retail subscription-based platform launched in 2017. The service provides IPO market data and research tools for individual investors, financial advisors, and professionals. The platform covers the U.S. IPO market.
IPO Center
IPO Center, which is part of the Renaissance Capital public website, provides free IPO information.
IPO ETFs
Renaissance Capital manages two exchange-traded funds listed on the New York Stock Exchange:
# Renaissance IPO ETF (NYSE: IPO) - Launched on October 14, 2013, the fund tracks the Renaissance IPO Index, which holds U.S.-listed companies that have recently completed initial public offerings.
# Renaissance International IPO ETF (NYSE: IPOS) – Launched on October 6, 2014, the fund tracks the Renaissance International IPO Index.
Both funds use a rules-based methodology with constituents weighted by float-adjusted market capitalization. Individual holdings are capped at 10% of the portfolio. The funds are rebalanced quarterly, with holdings remaining in the fund for three years. The funds are distributed by Foreside Fund Services, LLC.
IPO Data
Renaissance Capital provides IPO data through APIs and data feeds for institutional clients and developers.
Media Coverage
Renaissance Capital analysts are regularly quoted as sources on IPO market topics in financial media outlets including The Wall Street Journal, Bloomberg, CNBC, The New York Times, Forbes, Barron's, The Financial Times, and others. The firm's research and data are cited in coverage of IPO market trends and individual offerings.
American economist Jay Ritter, a leading authority on initial public offerings (IPOs), praised the firms research by saying Renaissance Capital "does first-rate research."
Scott Reeves, who covered IPOs for Barron's, said that "their research is excellent. They pretty much cover the waterfront and their picks are right on the money."
Joe Low, the managing director of Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette's investment banking division, said "these are quality people and they run a quality operation. I think they are very resourceful and have carved out a particular niche that I think over time will become increasingly important in the analysis of IPOs.
Scott Russo from Barron's said "Renaissance Capital offers stellar research... Their fund is very shrewd, as you would expect from a rat's nest of Wharton School graduates."
Investor's Business Daily called the firm "the 800-pound gorilla in IPO research and investment management."
Analysts from the firm have made numerous appearances on CNBC and other financial television networks to provide commentary on the IPO market. The Renaissance IPO Indices and ETFs are frequently used as a benchmark for the IPO market.
